title: st.multiselect no longer inserts the first filtered option on Enter (works in 1.49.1, not in 1.62.0)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In `st.multiselect`, typing a few letters and pressing Enter used to insert the first filtered option. Since the react-aria migration it inserts nothing: no option is marked as the user types, so Enter has nothing to commit and simply closes the list.

`st.selectbox` still commits its first filtered option on Enter, which is why this reads as an oversight rather than a decision, but I may be wrong about that and would rather ask than assume.

Filing it because the same migration produced #16003 (fuzzy search became contiguous-substring matching), which was accepted as a regression, and this is the same shape of quiet behaviour loss.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

picked = st.multiselect("Multi", ["Person", "Organization", "Department", "Role", "Project"])
st.write("multiselect:", picked)

one = st.selectbox("Single", ["Person", "Organization", "Role"], index=None)
st.write("selectbox:", one)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click the multiselect and type `Pe`.
2. Press Enter.
3. Do the same in the selectbox below it.

### Expected Behavior

Enter inserts `Person`, the first filtered option, as it did in 1.49.1 and as the selectbox still does in 1.62.0.

### Current Behavior

Enter clears the text and closes the list, and nothing is selected.

Comparing the same script on both versions, in the DOM after typing `Pe`:

| | 1.49.1 | 1.62.0 |
|---|---|---|
| options offered | Person, Project, Department | same (the fuzzy filter is unchanged) |
| first option | `aria-selected="true"`, tinted row | nothing marked, no `aria-activedescendant` |
| Enter | inserts Person | inserts nothing |
| extra row | none | `Select N matches`, keyed `__select_matches__` |
| selectbox, Enter | - | inserts the first option |

The arrow keys reach the option, but the first ArrowDown lands on the new `Select N matches` row, so the natural keyboard recovery (ArrowDown, Enter) selects *every* match rather than the one that was wanted. It takes ArrowDown twice.

I could not find a prop in React Aria's ComboBox for list autocomplete with automatic selection, so I appreciate this may not be a small change. The WAI-ARIA APG lists both automatic and manual selection as valid patterns, so this is a design question as much as a bug, which is why the question is in the summary.

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (working in 1.49.1)
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

Related: #16003 and #15438 (the BaseWeb to react-aria migration).

comments.body:
This is a keyboard regression in `st.multiselect` after the BaseWeb → React Aria ComboBox migration ([#16175](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16175), shipped in 1.61). RAC does not auto-focus a list item while typing (`focusedKey` stays null, no `aria-activedescendant`), so in **1.62.0** Enter is a no-op: the filter is cleared and the menu closes without selecting anything. `st.selectbox` still commits its first filtered option via a dedicated Enter handler, which is why the widgets now diverge.

**1.63.0** ([#16673](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16673)) replaced that no-op with “unfocused Enter commits the first visible row.” When two or more options match, that first row is `Select N matches` (`__select_matches__`), not the first option as in 1.49.1. Product approved this default; `select_all=False` restores type-then-Enter of the first match. Skipping the bulk row on Enter was explicitly rejected. A remaining gap is visual/ARIA highlighting: the first row is CSS-highlighted via `aria-posinset`, but RAC `focusedKey` / `aria-activedescendant` is still a TODO, so ArrowDown still lands on the bulk row first.

### Related Issues

- [#16537](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16537) — Same type-then-Enter vs “Select N matches” request. Closed by [#16673](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16673), which added `select_all=False` as the opt-out that restores first-match Enter.
- [#16003](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16003) — Cited by the reporter. Another quiet behavior loss from the React Aria ComboBox migration (selectbox fuzzy search), same class of regression.
- [#15697](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15697) — Open enhancement for customizable selectbox/multiselect keyboard navigation; related interaction surface, not a duplicate of this Enter/filter bug.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Hi [USER] - thanks for your thorough submission, it was very helpful!

Upgrading to `1.63.0` plus one parameter gets you the `1.49.1` behavior back:
```python
    st.multiselect("Multi", options, select_all=False)
```
Typing `Pe` then Enter inserts `Person`, as it used to.

Some background on why the parameter is needed. 1.63.0 changed Enter from a no-op to "commit the first visible row." When 2+ options match, that first row is `Select N matches` — so on the defaults, typing `Pe` (which fuzzy-matches Person, Project and Department) now selects all three, while typing `Per` (one match) inserts just `Person`. Enter activating the bulk row is the intended default rather than an oversight, and the new `select_all=False` is the opt-out that hides that row entirely. That came out of #16537.

Your second observation is the part that's still open, and you're right about it. 1.63.0 does mark the Enter target visually as you type — `Select 3 matches` on the defaults, or the first match with `select_all=False` — but nothing is exposed to assistive tech until you press an arrow key. The highlight is plain CSS on `[aria-posinset='1']`; React Aria's `focusedKey` is still null, so the input carries no
`aria-activedescendant` and no option carries `aria-selected="true"`. Press ArrowDown and ARIA catches up correctly, but that first ArrowDown lands on the bulk row, which is exactly why reaching the highlighted match takes two presses. In 1.49.1 the first filtered option carried `aria-selected="true"` while typing, so what regressed is specifically that a screen reader can no longer tell what Enter is about to do. `st.selectbox` is affected too, and slightly worse: it commits the first match on Enter with no highlight and no ARIA marking at all while typing.

So I'll keep this open for that accessibility gap.

Thanks [USER], that answers it, and the bulk row being the intended Enter target settles the design question rather than leaving it as an oversight.

I tested 1.63.0 against my own app before replying: a worktree at my current pin, a venv with 1.63.0, my Enter workaround removed, driven headless against a `Bulk Delete Classes` multiselect holding 58 class names. Typed `Ev`, pressed Enter.

| | Enter inserts | the app's armed warning |
|---|---|---|
| 1.62.0 + my workaround | `Event` | "This will delete 1 class(es)" |
| 1.63.0, defaults | `Event`, `EventType`, `ConcreteIndividual`, `ConcreteIndividualType` | "This will delete 4 class(es)" |
| 1.63.0, `select_all=False` | `Event` | "This will delete 1 class(es)" |

So `select_all=False` restores the 1.49.1 behaviour exactly. Thank you, that is the answer I needed.

The middle row is not a complaint about the default, just one data point on where it bites. The filter matches on subsequence, so `Ev` reaches `ConcreteIndividual` through the E in "Concrete" and the v in "Individual", and on the defaults a destructive picker arms four deletions for two keystrokes that used to mean one. I will pass `select_all=False` on those rather than leave it to muscle memory. It might be worth a line in the `select_all` docs saying that the bulk row is what Enter takes, since the widget looks the same either way.

The DOM matches your description exactly. After typing, `aria-activedescendant` is null and every row carries `aria-selected="false"`; `__select_matches__` sits at `aria-posinset="1"` on the defaults, and with `select_all=False` the first real option takes that slot.

On the accessibility half you are keeping open, two notes from having written the workaround, in case they are useful:

- Skipping the bulk row cannot be done by name. An empty box gives `__select_all__` and a typed query gives `__select_matches__`, so I match `/^__.*__$/` on `data-key` instead. "No results" is also a `[role="option"]`, and the only thing separating it from a real option is that it carries no `aria-selected` at all.
- The missing marking is what made the workaround delicate rather than trivial. With no `aria-activedescendant` and nothing `aria-selected="true"`, nothing in the DOM says what Enter is about to do, so the handler has to re-derive the target from option order. My guard for "react-aria has this covered, stand down" is the presence of `aria-activedescendant`, which is only correct because that attribute is absent in exactly the case that is broken. It is the same signal a screen reader is missing.

Happy to test a build once `focusedKey` is wired up.
